title: SL Catholics should not get deceived by impostors: Catholic Church in SL
byline: Sri Lankan Catholics should not be deceived by impostors, a spokesman from the Sri Lankan Church said.

title: US to delay weapons deliveries to some European countries due to Iran war
byline: U.S. officials have informed some ​European counterparts that some previously contracted weapons deliveries are likely to be delayed as the Iran war ‌continues to draw on weapons stocks, five sources familiar with the matter said.

title: Sinhala New Year rituals preserved for millennia under Buddhist guidance: Samarasinghe
byline: Sri Lankan Ambassador to the United States Mahinda Samarasinghe says that Sinhala New Year rituals, a cornerstone of the country’s cultural identity, have been preserved for thousands of years with Buddhist temples at their center and the guidance of Buddhist monks playing a significant historical role.

title: Major refinery fire won’t lead to fuel rationing, Australian PM says
byline: Fuel production at a critical Australian oil refinery has significantly dropped after a major fire but tougher restrictions will not be introduced, the country’s prime minister has said.

title: Grade 1 education reforms to be implemented in 2026
byline: The Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Ministry has announced that the implementation of Grade 1 education reforms for 2026 is currently underway.

title: Artemis II crew: ’We left as friends - we came back as best friends’
byline: The four astronauts of Artemis II say their mission gave the world a sense of hope and unity at a time when both feel in short supply.

title: Afternoon thundershowers forecast for several provinces
byline: Showers or thundershowers are expected to occur at several places in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Southern and Uva provinces, as well as in the Kandy and Nuwara Eliya districts after 1.00 p.m. today, the Meteorology Department said.

title: Presidential Commission appointed to probe coal procurement and power generation irregularities
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has appointed a fully fledged Presidential Commission of Inquiry to investigate alleged irregularities and illegal activities related to coal imports and electricity generation in Sri Lanka from the inception of coal-based power generation up to 16 April 2026.

title: Balagolla water plant supply restored for 16,977 Kundasale connections
byline: The National Water Supply and Drainage Board (NWSDB) says that the water supply scheme operated through the Balagolla Water Treatment Plant, which serves 16,977 water connections in the Kundasale Divisional Secretariat area, has now been restored following a temporary disruption.

title: Severe lightning and thundershowers likely in several districts after 1.00 p.m. – Met Department
byline: The Meteorology Department has issued a warning that thundershowers accompanied by severe lightning are likely at several places in the Southern Province as well as in Colombo, Kalutara, Monaragala, and Ratnapura districts after 1.00 p.m. today.

title: 150 kg of heroin seized from fishing vessel brought to Dikowita harbour
byline: Deputy Minister of Defence Aruna Jayasekara said that nearly 150 kilograms of heroin were recovered from a multi-day fishing vessel brought to the Dikowita Fisheries Harbour.

title: Bodies of two more victims recovered from Deduru Oya tragedy; Death toll rises to 8
byline: The bodies of the two remaining persons who drowned in the Deduru Oya in the Kobeigane area have now been recovered, police said.

title: Helicopter crash on Indonesia’s Borneo island kills 8
byline: A helicopter flying between palm oil plantations on Borneo Island crashed, killing the eight people on board, Indonesian officials said Friday.

title: Indian vice president to visit Sri Lanka on April 19–20
byline: The Vice President of India, C.P. Radhakrishnan, will undertake an official visit to Sri Lanka from April 19 to 20, 2026, marking the first-ever bilateral visit by an Indian Vice President to Sri Lanka, India External Affairs Ministry said.

title: One dead, two injured as car falls into 300-foot precipice in Balangoda
byline: A person was killed and two others sustained critical injuries after a car travelling from Balangoda to Kandy via Bagawanthalawa veered off the road and plunged into a 300-foot precipice near Keselgamu Oya on Friday (17), police said.

title: CPC denies $286 diesel import claims
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has firmly denied allegations that diesel was imported at USD 286 per barrel, with Managing Director Mayura Nethikumarage asserting that no crude oil or refined fuel was purchased at inflated prices and dismissing the reports as misleading.

title: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody resigns
byline: Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody and Ministry Secretary Professor Udayanga Hemapala tendered their resignations this afternoon to President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, the President’s Media Division  (PMD) said.

title: Temporary shade shelter set up in Jaffna to protect travelers from heat
byline: A temporary shade shelter made of sackcloth has been installed at the Thirunelveli signal junction in Jaffna by members of the Nallur Council.

title: Myanmar reduces ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi’s sentence, her lawyer says
byline: Myanmar has reduced the sentence of imprisoned ex-leader Aung San ​Suu Kyi, her lawyer told Reuters on Friday.

title: CPC ends QR-free fuel concession tomorrow midnight
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has announced that the temporary concession allowing petrol vehicle owners to obtain fuel without using a QR code will end at midnight tomorrow (18).

title: Catholic Church in Sri Lanka calls for an independent prosecution office
byline: The Catholic Church in Sri Lanka today called for the setting up of an independent prosecution office to ensure that those who are found responsible for the Easter Sunday bomb attacks could be dealt with effectively.

title: Is Central Bank enjoying special immunity? Ravi K
byline: MP Ravi Karunanayake who responded on the statement issued by the Central Bank if Sri Lanka (CBSL) that the NDB is safe despite the Rs 13.2 billion scam, questioned as to whether the former is enjoying special immunity.

title: Trump says Iran agreed to ‘never’ close Strait of Hormuz again
byline: The US president Donald Trump says Iran has “agreed to never close the Strait of Hormuz again.”

title: Iran says Hormuz open for commercial vessels after Lebanon ceasefire
byline: Iran on Friday said the Strait of Hormuz has been opened to all commercial vessels for the remaining duration of the ceasefire, stating that the move is in line with the Israel-Lebanon ceasefire agreement.

title: CSE extends rally for third consecutive session amid strengthening investor confidence
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange continued its upward trajectory on 17th April 2026, marking a third consecutive day of gains as improving global market conditions helped restore investor confidence.

title: Jayakody’s resignation too late, says Namal
byline: While criticising the resignation of Energy Minister Kumara Jayakody, Sri Lanka Podujana Peramuna (SLPP) National Organiser Namal Rajapaksa said the move comes far too late, despite it being accepted.

title: Sri Lanka among worst impacted countries in Asia-Pacific due to West Asia conflict: UN report
byline: The report published by the United Nations Development Programme, released on Thursday, provides a preliminary assessment on how the ongoing conflict is destabilising global trade, energy markets, and financial systems.

title: Oil falls by 11% after Iran’s foreign minister declares Strait of Hormuz open
byline: Oil prices plunged by about 11% on Friday, extending earlier losses, after Iran’s foreign minister said ​that passage for all commercial vessels through the Strait of ‌Hormuz was open for the remaining ceasefire period.

title: Myanmar reduces ex-leader Aung San Suu Kyi’s sentence, her lawyer says
byline: Myanmar has reduced the sentence of imprisoned ex-leader Aung San ​Suu Kyi, her lawyer told Reuters on Friday.
